QuestionStmt.S: If a random variable $X$ follows the Binomial distribution $B(33, p)$ such that $3P(X = 0) = P(X = 1)$, then the variance of $X$ is

Solution.S:
For a binomial distribution $B(n, p)$ with $n = 33$, we have $P(X = r) = \binom{n}{r} p^r q^{n-r}$, where $q = 1-p$.

Given: $3P(X = 0) = P(X = 1)$.

$$3 \cdot \binom{33}{0} p^0 q^{33} = \binom{33}{1} p^1 q^{32}$$

$$3 \cdot 1 \cdot q^{33} = 33 \cdot p \cdot q^{32}$$

Cancel $q^{32}$ (since $q > 0$):

$$3q = 33p \quad \Rightarrow \quad p = \frac{1}{11} q$$

Now $p + q = 1$, so $\frac{1}{11}q + q = 1 \Rightarrow \frac{12}{11}q = 1 \Rightarrow q = \frac{11}{12}$.

Then $p = 1 - q = \frac{1}{12}$.

Variance of binomial distribution: $\text{Var}(X) = n p q = 33 \times \frac{1}{12} \times \frac{11}{12} = \frac{33 \times 11}{144} = \frac{363}{144} = \frac{121}{48}$.

Thus the correct option is C: $\frac{121}{48}$.
